reason: The contract (problem.txt) requires each output to equal the real-valued sigmoid rounded exactly once to IEEE binary16 RNE, with "Exact FP16 bit patterns ... must hold for the whole public domain" and "One failing legal input is evidence against the implementation." Probe t9 exhaustively scanned all 63,488 finite FP16 encodings (the entire legal per-element domain) and found 7 legal inputs — e.g. x=0.0029296875 (kernel bits 14338 vs correct 14337), x=-0.00927734375 (14326 vs 14327) — where run() produces a one-ULP-wrong FP16 bit pattern. At every mismatch the FP64 reference matches the longdouble-computed true RNE rounding, and c3's probe shows no input's true sigmoid lies anywhere near an FP16 tie (min relative tie distance ~5.5e-4), so the mismatches are genuine kernel double-rounding errors, not reference-precision or tie-ambiguity artifacts. c2 (probe t10) confirms the mechanism: libdevice.exp's FP32 rounding error alone flips the final FP16 rounding. The contract's "any internal precision is permitted if the final FP16 output satisfies this requirement" clause makes internal FP32 precision no excuse; the exact-rounding requirement is a declared numeric format whose violation is a defect regardless of deviation size. This is not an unspecified-tie or contract-permitted-variation case. Reject.
